outcome: Zauner's conjecture remains open. The most substantial development is a January 2025 preprint (Appleby, Flammia, Kopp) giving an explicit construction of SICs in every dimension d>3, valid conditional on the order-1 abelian Stark conjecture for real quadratic fields and a new 'Twisted Convolution Conjecture' the authors introduce — this reduces Zauner's conjecture to other open conjectures rather than proving it. A January 2026 preprint (Stefan Joka) claiming a full unconditional proof for all finite dimensions was found flawed on review (a false vertex identification and circular induction) and was withdrawn by the author himself in a fifth revision in May 2026. A September 2026 preprint (McConnell) proves a structure theorem for SIC dimension towers, a further piece of number-theoretic scaffolding, not a resolution.

disputes.summary: Stefan Joka's arXiv:2601.13475 (submitted 20 Jan 2026) claimed a full unconditional proof that SIC-POVMs exist in every finite dimension. Reviewers (per pith.science's review of the paper) found that the central identification between moment-polytope vertices and rank-one projectors is false and that the paper's induction argument is circular. The paper went through five revisions (v1 20 Jan 2026, v2 22 Jan 2026, v3 7 Feb 2026, v4 7 Mar 2026, v5 31 May 2026) and was ultimately withdrawn by the author in v5, with the withdrawal itself confirming 'the proof the paper gives is not correct.'

summary: Zauner's conjecture (do SIC-POVMs exist in all finite dimensions?) is still open as of September 2026, and I found no evidence that any AI system contributed to any of the mathematics attempted on it in this window. The genuinely substantial event is Appleby, Flammia and Kopp's 'A Constructive Approach to Zauner's Conjecture via the Stark Conjectures' (arXiv:2501.03970, submitted 7 Jan 2025, revised to v2 17 Mar 2025). It gives an explicit construction — a 'ghost SIC' built from real-multiplication values of the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle — that the authors prove yields a valid SIC in every dimension d>3, but only conditional on (1) the order-1 abelian Stark conjecture for real quadratic fields, itself a major open conjecture in number theory, and (2) a new identity they call the Twisted Convolution Conjecture, whose difficulty a third-party review (pith.science) notes 'may be comparable to the target result' itself. Because Zauner's conjecture is not proved outright, and because the reduction is to other unproved conjectures (not a restriction to a sub-case), I classify this as `progress` rather than `partial` or `claimed`: it is a structural advance / conditional roadmap, not a settled case of the stated existence question. No AI involvement is mentioned anywhere in the paper, on ResearchGate, or in third-party commentary I found. Separately, a January 2026 preprint by Stefan Joka (arXiv:2601.13475) claimed a full unconditional proof for every finite dimension; this is the kind of dramatic claim that would matter a great deal if correct, but expert review (via pith.science, a paper-review aggregator) identified a false identification between moment-polytope vertices and rank-one projectors and a circular induction step, and the author withdrew the paper himself after five revisions spanning January-May 2026 — the arXiv withdrawal notice states plainly 'the proof the paper gives is not correct.' This is recorded as the instructive-failure branch of `progress` (an announced/preprinted claim that came to nothing), dated to the original claim (20 Jan 2026) per §6.1's rule for incidents, though I use ai_role `none` (not `incident`) because there is no evidence any AI system was involved in producing or checking Joka's proof — it appears to be an ordinary (mistaken) human mathematics preprint, not an AI-produced claim. A third paper, Gary McConnell's 'SIC dimension towers via cyclotomic polynomials' (arXiv:2609.04431, submitted 3 Sep 2026), proves a structure theorem situating the known SIC dimension towers within a broader cyclotomic/arithmetic framework; it neither resolves any case nor moves a numerical bound on the conjecture itself, so on its own it would not even rise to `progress`, but the overall problem status of `progress` is carried by the Appleby-Flammia-Kopp reduction. I found nothing suggesting the January 2024 Wikipedia lead ('do SIC-POVMs exist in all dimensions?') needs updating: SIC-POVMs are still only known/verified in specific dimensions (exact solutions to d=53 and scattered higher values, numerical solutions further out), and the general existence question is unresolved.
competing_reading: One could argue the Appleby-Flammia-Kopp paper deserves `claimed` rather than `progress`, on the reasoning that it is a nearly-complete proof modulo well-regarded, independently-motivated number-theoretic conjectures (the Stark conjectures have their own long history and community credibility) — under that reading it is closer to 'a proof, conditional on X' being treated as a serious claim awaiting X. I did not adopt this because the paper's own second condition, the Twisted Convolution Conjecture, is new and unproved elsewhere, is acknowledged by reviewers as possibly as hard as the target, and Zauner's conjecture itself is not asserted to be proved by any human expert digestion I found — the paper's own framing is constructive/conditional rather than a claimed resolution.
what_would_settle_it: A proof of the order-1 abelian Stark conjecture for real quadratic fields, or of the Twisted Convolution Conjecture, that experts accept as closing Appleby-Flammia-Kopp's construction — or any independent unconditional proof of Zauner's conjecture that survives expert review (which Joka's attempt did not).
